page: Google Cloud Platform x5-688-12t-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized compute instance designed for extreme-scale memory footprints. The system features 688 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and provides 12,288 GB (12 TB) of system memory. This configuration yields a high memory density of approximately 17.86 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing it far beyond standard memory-optimized tiers.

Hardware allocation is strictly dedicated, offering bare-metal access without hypervisor overhead. The instance does not bundle local disk storage, requiring external persistent storage solutions for stateful operations. In addition, it contains zero GPUs and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, focusing purely on massive CPU parallelism and central memory capacity.

From an architectural standpoint, the server is tailored for monolithic, memory-bound workloads that cannot easily be distributed across clusters. Delivering substantial resource density in a single node, it maximizes cost efficiency by eliminating multi-node clustering overhead and hypervisor penalties for scale-up architectures. Primary workload targets include very large in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, enterprise ERP backbones, and large-scale data caches.
description: Google Cloud Platform x5-688-12t-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance featuring 688 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 12,288 GB of RAM. Designed for extreme-scale architectures, it delivers a dense ratio of approximately 17.86 GB of memory per core. The server includes no bundled local storage, no hardware GPU accelerators, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network storage for disk operations. This bare-metal setup removes virtualization layers, maximizing raw compute efficiency and throughput across its substantial CPU footprint. The platform is best suited for monolithic, memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as massive in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, complex real-time data analytics, and mission-critical ERP systems requiring massive memory capacity on a single node.
